title: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder And Inorder Traversal
description: Reconstruct a binary tree by splitting each inorder traversal around the root found at the start of its preorder traversal.
note: Use copying slices to pass the left and right traversal segments into recursive calls.
notes: Assume valid matching traversals with distinct values. Empty traversals produce none. The algorithm preserves the traversal order; the reconstructed tree need not be a binary search tree.

List index(value) returns int? and identifies the first matching position, including zero. Valid traversals guarantee a match, so mid can be used directly in arithmetic and slice bounds through checked optional use. An absent match would fail when an integer position is required.

Slices include the start and exclude the end. inorder[:mid] excludes the root, and preorder[1:mid + 1] contains exactly mid nodes. An omitted start is zero and an omitted end is the source size. Empty subtrees naturally use equal-bound or empty suffix slices.

TreeNode(value, left, right) uses the generated record constructor in field order. This constructs the children directly instead of allocating a node and assigning its fields afterward. The Python reference uses the same structure.

Slices create fresh outer lists and index lookup does not mutate its receiver. Neither input traversal is modified. LeetCode supplies TreeNode; the record declaration shows its standalone Birdie form.

This keeps the simpler slicing algorithm. Under copying-slice semantics, worst-case time and auxiliary slice storage are O(n^2) on a skewed tree. The recursion uses O(h) stack space and the output has O(n) nodes.
